goal.statement: Use synthetic players to catch broken mechanics and balance regressions before human playtests, then use humans to judge whether the game is actually fun.
goal.human_outcome: Players get a fairer, more legible and more enjoyable game with fewer obvious balance failures.

state.current: Agent Lab Core already provides deterministic matches, replay verification, conformance tests, tournaments and paired counterfactuals.

gap.blocker: There is no studio-level release gate separating what simulation can prove from what only human play can prove.
gap.why_now: Cheaper long-horizon agents and reusable game adapters make thousands of reproducible synthetic sessions practical before every human test.

options: Run simulation gates first, then targeted human playtests

decision.selected_path: Run simulation gates first, then targeted human playtests
decision.rationale: Machines are excellent at repetition, edge cases and reproducibility; humans remain the authority on enjoyment, clarity, attachment and meaning.

action.next_action: Connect one live studio game to Agent Lab Core and run baseline-versus-patch simulation with a human playtest handoff.

success_metrics: dominant strategy and patch deltas are surfaced
human playtest records enjoyment, clarity and replay intent separately
stop_conditions: simulation results are presented as proof of fun
patch creates a critical rules regression
human feedback shows the simulated improvement harmed enjoyment

feedback.next_cycle_trigger: Simulation or human evidence changes the patch, tutorial, balance or release decision.
